rules.sentence: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a type of pulmonary hypertension (PH) characterized by increased resistance in the pulmonary circulation, which is caused by progressive pulmonary artery remodeling and constriction of the pulmonary vasculature.[1][2]
In the current era of PAH management, one-year survival rates have increased to 86% to 90% from 65% in the 1980s, and average long-term survival has increased to 6 years from 2.8 years.[3]
Due to the self-resolving nature of PLEVA, follow-up visits should occur every 3 to 6 months if there is no desire for treatment.
